decision: Keep production MiniLM unchanged. The initial instruction-reranker policy has one development-only complete-answer gain and no regression in 5,796 compared views. Heldout has no gains. Lower-cutoff calibration fails 11 historical negative cases. Current application backend cannot run this export; footprint and absent heldout improvement do not justify integration.

onnx_export.provenance: Community mixed-precision export; graph bytes pinned to repository LFS hash. Not the official upstream ONNX artifact.

native_runtime.scope: Isolated evaluation package only. Existing Tract/BERT application backend does not support this graph/interface. No production dependency/default/download/release change.

model.instruction: Given a coding task, retrieve a stored memory fact only if it directly answers the task or provides the required corrective action. Reject facts that are merely about the same broad topic.
model.instruction_template: Official prefix + separately tokenized <Instruct>, <Query>, <Document> body + official assistant empty-think suffix; no padding, no silent clipping, research cap512 tokens.
model.score: Last-position yes logit minus no logit. Probability is sigmoid(log_odds); labels come from pinned tokenizer. No generated text or pooled embeddings.
model.pool: Reuse all previously frozen label-independent MiniLM primary pools, capped32 (actual maximum20, no truncation). No gold insertion or altered source facts.
model.admission: Empty MiniLM results without query files only. Rank candidate source records by log_odds then UUID. Require runner-up, winning log_odds floor and top-minus-second log_odds margin floor. Append at most one winning record only when its actual native packet preview accepts it.
model.selection: Original/fresh/new development only. Require unchanged per-record comparator AND no added positive IDs outside required source facts. Labels are scoring audits only, never admission features. Maximize safe complete-answer gains; ties higher log_odds then higher margin. Any candidate requires historical development then heldout and native application backend compatibility before production consideration.
model.reference_gate: Before fixture inference, require finite bounded outputs and yes probability >0.5 for both official README positive pairs, <0.5 for their crossed negatives, correct ordering for each query. These are behavioral references; no independent numerical Q4 versus upstream PyTorch parity is claimed.
model.fallback: On reference failure or no safe gain, reject and leave heldout unscored. Preserve all fixtures and gates.

execution.prefix_reuse: Group exactly equal queries, compute exact common token prefix across their frozen candidate prompts. Prefill once; reuse its immutable float32 KV tensors with full attention length and absolute position offsets. No prefix or suffix clipping.
execution.fixture_equivalence_audit: After benchmark, rescore the first eight pair IDs in lexicographic SHA-256 order using full uncached prefill; require log_odds agreement within .001. Also audit threshold/rank boundaries within .001 before accepting a gain.

reference-result.json.scope: Behavioral references only; no independent numerical upstream/quantization parity.

checks.clippy: Both changed Rust example targets separately, warnings denied
checks.formatting: Changed Rust, JSON and Markdown checked

limitations: One exposed development question improves; heldout questions do not improve.
Native CPU ONNX Runtime evaluation is separate from the application Tract/BERT backend.
Q4 community conversion has behavioral references and cache/uncached checks, not independent numerical upstream PyTorch parity.
These are synthetic correlated retrieval cases, not capture or live-agent task evidence.
No-match labels include assistant-authored judgments, not independently judged precision.
Input cap512, pool cap32, empty/no-files admission; no general long-input or nonempty-result rescue claim.
No probability-calibration claim: scores are ranking signals and accepted log odds can be negative.
